         private companion object {
             const val KEY_UID = "uid"
             const val KEY_PHONE_LAST_FOUR = "phone_last_four"
             const val KEY_SESSION_CREATED_AT = "session_created_at_epoch_ms"
             const val KEY_EMAIL = "email"
             const val KEY_DISPLAY_NAME = "display_name"
             const val KEY_AUTH_PROVIDER = "auth_provider"
             const val KEY_ONBOARDING_COMPLETE_LEGACY = "onboarding_complete"
             const val KEY_ONBOARDING_COMPLETE_PREFIX = "onboarding_complete_"
             val SESSION_TTL_MS = TimeUnit.DAYS.toMillis(180)
         }
 
         private val _authState = MutableStateFlow(readInitialState())
         public val authState: StateFlow<AuthState> = _authState.asStateFlow()
 
         public val isOnboardingComplete: Boolean
             get() {
                 val uid = currentUid() ?: return false
                 return prefs.getBoolean(onboardingCompleteKey(uid), false)
             }
 
         public suspend fun setOnboardingComplete() {
             withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                 val uid = currentUid() ?: return@withContext
                 prefs
                     .edit()
                     .putBoolean(onboardingCompleteKey(uid), true)
                     .remove(KEY_ONBOARDING_COMPLETE_LEGACY)
                     .apply()
             }
         }
 
         private fun readInitialState(): AuthState {
             val uid = prefs.getString(KEY_UID, null)
             val createdAt = prefs.getLong(KEY_SESSION_CREATED_AT, 0L)
             val sessionExpired =
                 uid == null ||
                     createdAt == 0L ||
                     System.currentTimeMillis() - createdAt > SESSION_TTL_MS
             return if (sessionExpired) {
                 if (uid != null) clearSessionPrefs()
                 AuthState.Unauthenticated
             } else {
                 AuthState.Authenticated(
                     uid = uid!!,
                     phoneLastFour = prefs.getString(KEY_PHONE_LAST_FOUR, null),
                     email = prefs.getString(KEY_EMAIL, null),
                     displayName = prefs.getString(KEY_DISPLAY_NAME, null),
                     authProvider = parseProvider(prefs.getString(KEY_AUTH_PROVIDER, null)),
                 )
             }
         }
 
         private fun parseProvider(raw: String?): AuthProvider =
             when (raw) {
                 "google" -> AuthProvider.Google
                 "email" -> AuthProvider.Email
                 else -> AuthProvider.Phone
             }
 
         private fun providerKey(provider: AuthProvider): String =
             when (provider) {
                 AuthProvider.Phone -> "phone"
                 AuthProvider.Google -> "google"
                 AuthProvider.Email -> "email"
             }
 
         public suspend fun saveSession(
             uid: String,
             phoneLastFour: String? = null,
             email: String? = null,
             displayName: String? = null,
             authProvider: AuthProvider = AuthProvider.Phone,
         ) {
             withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
                 val legacyOnboardingComplete = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_ONBOARDING_COMPLETE_LEGACY, false)
                 val editor =
                     prefs
                         .edit()
                         .putString(KEY_UID, uid)
                         .putString(KEY_AUTH_PROVIDER, providerKey(authProvider))
                         .putLong(KEY_SESSION_CREATED_AT, System.currentTimeMillis())
                 if (phoneLastFour != null) {
                     editor.putString(KEY_PHONE_LAST_FOUR, phoneLastFour)
                 } else {
                     editor.remove(KEY_PHONE_LAST_FOUR)
                 }
                 if (email != null) {
                     editor.putString(KEY_EMAIL, email)
                 } else {
                     editor.remove(KEY_EMAIL)
                 }
                 if (displayName != null) {
                     editor.putString(KEY_DISPLAY_NAME, displayName)
                 } else {
                     editor.remove(KEY_DISPLAY_NAME)
                 }
                 if (legacyOnboardingComplete) {
                     editor
                         .putBoolean(onboardingCompleteKey(uid), true)
                         .remove(KEY_ONBOARDING_COMPLETE_LEGACY)
                 }
                 editor.apply()
             }
             _authState.value =
                 AuthState.Authenticated(
                     uid = uid,
                     phoneLastFour = phoneLastFour,
                     email = email,
                     displayName = displayName,
                     authProvider = authProvider,
                 )
         }
 
         public suspend fun clearSession() {
+            // Capture uid BEFORE clearing prefs so it's available for the server unregister call.
+            val uid = currentUid()
             withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { clearSessionPrefs() }
             _authState.value = AuthState.Unauthenticated
+            // Best-effort server device-token unregister — never blocks sign-out.
+            if (uid != null) {
+                runCatching { deviceTokenRegistrar.unregister() }
+            }
         }
 
         private fun currentUid(): String? {
             val fromState = (authState.value as? AuthState.Authenticated)?.uid
             return fromState ?: prefs.getString(KEY_UID, null)
         }
 
         private fun onboardingCompleteKey(uid: String): String = "$KEY_ONBOARDING_COMPLETE_PREFIX$uid"
 
         private fun clearSessionPrefs() {
             prefs
                 .edit()
                 .remove(KEY_UID)
                 .remove(KEY_PHONE_LAST_FOUR)
                 .remove(KEY_SESSION_CREATED_AT)
                 .remove(KEY_EMAIL)
                 .remove(KEY_DISPLAY_NAME)
                 .remove(KEY_AUTH_PROVIDER)
                 .remove(KEY_ONBOARDING_COMPLETE_LEGACY)
                 .apply()
         }
     }

     @Provides

     public fun provideCredentialManager(

     @Provides
     @Singleton
     @AuthPrefs
     public fun provideAuthPrefs(
         @ApplicationContext context: Context,
     ): SharedPreferences {
         val masterKey =
             MasterKey
                 .Builder(context)
                 .setKeyScheme(MasterKey.KeyScheme.AES256_GCM)
                 .build()
         val prefs =
             EncryptedSharedPreferences.create(
                 context,
                 "tech_auth_session",
                 masterKey,
                 EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefKeyEncryptionScheme.AES256_SIV,
                 EncryptedSharedPreferences.PrefValueEncryptionScheme.AES256_GCM,
             )
         // Silently migrate any session data written by the deprecated MasterKeys API.
         // No-op if legacy key alias is absent (first install or already migrated).
         SessionPrefsMigrator.migrateIfNeeded(context, prefs, "tech_auth_session")
         return prefs
     }
 }

18:
19:@Qualifier
20:@Retention(AnnotationRetention.BINARY)
21:public annotation class AuthOkHttpClient
22:
23:@Qualifier
24:@Retention(AnnotationRetention.BINARY)
25:public annotation class UnauthOkHttpClient
26:
27:@Module
28:@InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class)
29:public object NetworkModule {
30:    @Provides
31:    @Singleton
32:    public fun provideMoshi(): Moshi = defaultMoshi
33:
34:    @Provides
35:    @Singleton
36:    public fun provideLoggingInterceptor(): HttpLoggingInterceptor =
37:        HttpLoggingInterceptor().apply {
38:            level =
39:                if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) {
40:                    HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY
41:                } else {
42:                    HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.NONE
43:                }
44:        }
45:
46:    @Provides
47:    @Singleton
48:    @AuthOkHttpClient
49:    public fun provideAuthOkHttpClient(
50:        idTokenCache: IdTokenCache,
51:        authenticator: FirebaseTokenAuthenticator,
52:        logging: HttpLoggingInterceptor,
53:    ): OkHttpClient =
54:        OkHttpClient
55:            .Builder()
56:            .addInterceptor { chain ->
57:                val token = idTokenCache.cachedToken
58:                val req =
59:                    if (token != null) {
60:                        chain
61:                            .request()
62:                            .newBuilder()
63:                            .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
64:                            .build()
65:                    } else {
66:                        chain.request()
67:                    }
68:                chain.proceed(req)
69:            }.addInterceptor(logging)
70:            .authenticator(authenticator)
71:            .build()
72:
73:    @Provides
74:    @Singleton
75:    @UnauthOkHttpClient
76:    public fun provideUnauthOkHttpClient(logging: HttpLoggingInterceptor): OkHttpClient =
77:        OkHttpClient
78:            .Builder()
79:            .addInterceptor(logging)
80:            .build()
81:
82:    @Provides
83:    @Singleton
84:    public fun provideRetrofit(
85:        @AuthOkHttpClient client: OkHttpClient,
86:        moshi: Moshi,
87:    ): Retrofit =
88:        Retrofit
89:            .Builder()
90:            .baseUrl(BuildConfig.API_BASE_URL + "/")
91:            .client(client)
92:            .addConverterFactory(MoshiConverterFactory.create(moshi))
93:            .build()
94:}

3:import android.util.Log
4:import com.google.firebase.auth.FirebaseAuth
5:import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
6:import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers

11:import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
12:import javax.inject.Inject
13:import javax.inject.Singleton

15:/**
16: * Singleton cache for Firebase ID tokens (technician-app).
17: *
18: * Background refresh every 55 minutes. Also invalidates synchronously on auth state
19: * changes (sign-in / sign-out / user switch) â€” critical because the `cachedToken` is
20: * read by the @AuthOkHttpClient interceptor without consulting `FirebaseAuth.currentUser`
21: * per request. Without invalidation, the first request after a sign-out â†’ sign-in
22: * transition would send the *previous* user's bearer with the *new* user's payload
23: * (cross-account leak; see Codex review W1 round 1).
24: *
25: * See customer-app's [com.homeservices.customer.data.network.auth.IdTokenCache] for the
26: * shared design rationale.
27: */
28:@Singleton
29:public class IdTokenCache
30:    @Inject
31:    constructor(
32:        private val firebaseAuth: FirebaseAuth,
33:    ) {
34:        private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO)
35:
36:        @Volatile
37:        public var cachedToken: String? = null
38:            private set
39:
40:        init {
41:            scope.launch { refreshLoop() }
42:            // Invalidate on auth state change: sign-out â†’ drop stale token; sign-in â†’
43:            // fetch fresh token for the new user. The listener fires immediately with
44:            // the current user (or null), which is fine â€” the refreshLoop's first
45:            // iteration will populate cachedToken either way.
46:            firebaseAuth.addAuthStateListener { auth ->
47:                cachedToken = null
48:                if (auth.currentUser != null) {
49:                    scope.launch { freshToken() }
50:                }
51:            }
52:        }
53:
54:        public suspend fun freshToken(): String? {
55:            return try {
56:                val user = firebaseAuth.currentUser ?: return null
57:                val startUid = user.uid
58:                val result = user.getIdToken(false).await()
59:                val token = result?.token
60:                // Fence: if the signed-in user changed while we were awaiting the
61:                // token fetch, discard this result rather than overwriting the cache
62:                // with a stale bearer. The AuthStateListener will have already
63:                // launched a fresh freshToken() for the new user; we'd be racing
64:                // against it (Codex review W1 round 2 [P2]).
65:                if (firebaseAuth.currentUser?.uid == startUid) {
66:                    cachedToken = token
67:                    token
68:                } else {
69:                    Log.w(TAG, "IdToken result discarded: user changed during fetch")
70:                    null
71:                }
72:            } catch (e: Exception) {
73:                Log.w(TAG, "IdToken fetch failed", e)
74:                null
75:            }
76:        }
77:
78:        private suspend fun refreshLoop() {
79:            while (true) {
80:                freshToken()
81:                delay(REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS)
82:            }
83:        }
84:
85:        private companion object {
86:            const val TAG = "TechIdTokenCache"
87:            val REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = TimeUnit.MINUTES.toMillis(55)
88:        }
89:    }

60:                val user =
61:                    result.user ?: return AuthResult.Error.General(
62:                        IllegalStateException("null user after anonymous sign-in"),
63:                    )
64:                val lastFour = phoneNumber.takeLast(PHONE_LAST_DIGITS)
65:                sessionManager.saveSession(
66:                    uid = user.uid,
67:                    phoneLastFour = lastFour,
68:                    authProvider = AuthProvider.Phone,
69:                )

71:            } catch (e: FirebaseException) {
72:                AuthResult.Error.General(e)
73:            }
74:        }

157:                        }

164:                    },

166:            }
167:            onboardingGraph(navController, sessionManager, scope)
168:            homeGraph(

36:
37:@Composable
38:internal fun AppNavigation(
39:    sessionManager: SessionManager,
40:    activity: FragmentActivity,
41:    ratingPromptEventBus: RatingPromptEventBus,
42:    ratingReceivedEventBus: RatingReceivedEventBus,
43:    fcmTopicSubscriber: FcmTopicSubscriber,
44:    fcmTokenSyncUseCase: FcmTokenSyncUseCase,
45:    coldStartNavDestination: String? = null,
46:    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
47:): Unit {
48:    val navController = rememberNavController()
49:    val context = LocalContext.current
50:    val authState by sessionManager.authState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
51:    val jobOfferViewModel: JobOfferViewModel = hiltViewModel()
52:    val jobOfferState by jobOfferViewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
53:    val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
54:    val notificationPermissionLauncher =
55:        rememberLauncherForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission()) {
56:            // The dispatch token is synced independently; Android controls notification display.
57:        }
58:
59:    LaunchedEffect(authState) {
60:        val current = authState
61:        when (current) {
62:            is AuthState.Authenticated -> {
63:                val dest = if (sessionManager.isOnboardingComplete) "home" else "onboarding_gate"
64:                navController.navigate(dest) {
65:                    popUpTo("auth") { inclusive = true }
66:                    launchSingleTop = true
67:                }
68:                fcmTopicSubscriber.subscribeTechnician(current.uid)
69:                if (!context.hasNotificationPermission()) {
70:                    notificationPermissionLauncher.launch(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS)
71:                }
72:                fcmTokenSyncUseCase()
73:            }
74:            is AuthState.Unauthenticated -> {
75:                // Drain any buffered rating prompts so the next technician to
76:                // log in on this device can't be routed into the previous
77:                // technician's pending booking flow.
78:                ratingPromptEventBus.clearBuffered()
79:                ratingReceivedEventBus.clearBuffered()
80:                fcmTopicSubscriber.unsubscribeTechnician()
81:                navController.navigate("auth") {
82:                    popUpTo("main") { inclusive = true }
83:                    launchSingleTop = true
84:                }
85:            }
86:        }
87:    }
88:
89:    LaunchedEffect(jobOfferState) {
90:        if (jobOfferState is JobOfferUiState.Accepted) {
91:            val bookingId = (jobOfferState as JobOfferUiState.Accepted).bookingId
92:            navController.navigate("activeJob/$bookingId") {
93:                launchSingleTop = true
94:            }
95:        }

13:export function requireAdmin(roles: AdminRole[]) {
14:  return (handler: AdminHttpHandler): HttpHandler =>
15:    async (req: HttpRequest, ctx: InvocationContext): Promise<HttpResponseInit> => {
16:      const cookies = parseCookies(req.headers.get('cookie') ?? undefined);
17:      const token = cookies['hs_access'];

19:

22:
23:      const session = await touchAndGetSession(payload.sessionId);
24:      if (!session) return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'SESSION_EXPIRED' } };
25:
26:      const role = normalizeAdminRole(payload.role);
27:      if (!role) return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'TOKEN_INVALID' } };
28:
29:      if (!roles.includes(role)) {
30:        return { status: 403, jsonBody: { code: 'FORBIDDEN', requiredRoles: roles } };
31:      }
32:
33:      return handler(req, ctx, {
34:        adminId: payload.sub,
35:        role,
36:        sessionId: payload.sessionId,
37:      });
38:    };
39:}

docs/reviews/codex-e11-s05b-2-round7-20260518-0426.md:4117:docs/stories/E07-S05-safety-sos.md:246:**FCM owner topic:** The existing `fcm.service.ts` uses topic `'owner_alerts'` (not `'owner_ops'`). All owner FCM messages go to this topic. Add `sendOwnerSosAlert` as a new exported function following the exact same pattern as `sendOwnerRatingShieldAlert`.
docs/reviews/codex-e11-s05b-2-round7-20260518-0426.md:4118:docs/stories/E07-S05-safety-sos.md:264:**No technician-app changes:** Technician must not see the SOS trigger or receive any FCM related to it. The `owner_alerts` topic is owner-only.
docs/reviews/codex-e11-s05b-2-round7-20260518-0426.md:4119:docs/stories/E07-S05-safety-sos.md:346:**Why `owner_alerts` not `owner_ops`:** The FCM service currently has no `owner_ops` topic. All owner alerts (rating shield, recon mismatch, and now SOS) flow through `'owner_alerts'`. If the intent was to separate operational vs. safety alerts in future, that would need a new topic registered in Firebase and a separate admin FCM subscription — out of scope for this story.

docs/stories/E07-S05-safety-sos.md:246:**FCM owner topic:** The existing `fcm.service.ts` uses topic `'owner_alerts'` (not `'owner_ops'`). All owner FCM messages go to this topic. Add `sendOwnerSosAlert` as a new exported function following the exact same pattern as `sendOwnerRatingShieldAlert`.
docs/stories/E07-S05-safety-sos.md:264:**No technician-app changes:** Technician must not see the SOS trigger or receive any FCM related to it. The `owner_alerts` topic is owner-only.
docs/stories/E07-S05-safety-sos.md:346:**Why `owner_alerts` not `owner_ops`:** The FCM service currently has no `owner_ops` topic. All owner alerts (rating shield, recon mismatch, and now SOS) flow through `'owner_alerts'`. If the intent was to separate operational vs. safety alerts in future, that would need a new topic registered in Firebase and a separate admin FCM subscription — out of scope for this story.

1:import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
2:import { userDataCascadeWrites } from '../cosmos/user-data-cascade-writes.js';
3:import type { ErasureDeletedCounts, ErasureRequestDoc } from '../schemas/erasure-request.js';
4:
5:/**
6: * Computes the irreversible anonymized hash from uid + per-request salt.
7: * SHA-256 hex (64 chars). The salt is the only mechanism that links the
8: * hash back to the natural-person uid â€” and only if regulatory hold
9: * required us to retain it.
10: */
11:export function computeAnonymizedHash(uid: string, salt: string): string {
12:  return createHash('sha256').update(`${uid}:${salt}`).digest('hex');
13:}
14:
15:/**
16: * Executes the DPDP Â§12 cascade for a single erasure request.
17: *
18: * Caller MUST have already transitioned the request to EXECUTING and persisted
19: * the anonymizedHash (so admin retries are idempotent: each step's natural
20: * predicate ("rows where customerId = uid") becomes a no-op once executed).
21: *
22: * Each cosmos cross-container step is independently retryable. Failures here
23: * propagate up to the caller, which marks the request FAILED and may retry.
24: */
25:export async function executeErasureCascade(
26:  request: Pick<ErasureRequestDoc, 'userId' | 'userRole' | 'anonymizationSalt'>,
27:): Promise<ErasureDeletedCounts> {
28:  const { userId, userRole, anonymizationSalt } = request;
29:  const hash = computeAnonymizedHash(userId, anonymizationSalt);
30:
31:  // Anonymize across containers in parallel â€” they target disjoint containers.
32:  const [
33:    bookings,
34:    ratings,
35:    complaints,
36:    walletLedgerAnonymized,
37:    bookingEventsAnonymized,
38:    dispatchAttemptsAnonymized,
39:    auditLogAnonymized,
40:  ] = await Promise.all([
41:    userDataCascadeWrites.anonymizeBookings(userId, hash),
42:    userDataCascadeWrites.anonymizeRatings(userId, hash),
43:    userDataCascadeWrites.anonymizeComplaints(userId, hash),
44:    userRole === 'TECHNICIAN'
45:      ? userDataCascadeWrites.anonymizeWalletLedger(userId, hash)
46:      : Promise.resolve(0),
47:    userDataCascadeWrites.anonymizeBookingEvents(userId, hash),
48:    userDataCascadeWrites.anonymizeDispatchAttempts(userId, hash),
49:    userDataCascadeWrites.anonymizeAuditLogResourceId(userId, hash),
50:  ]);
51:
52:  let technicianHardDeleted = false;
53:  let kycHardDeleted = false;
54:  let fcmTokensCleared = false;
55:
56:  if (userRole === 'TECHNICIAN') {
57:    // Clear FCM token before hard-delete (so the doc still exists for the patch).
58:    fcmTokensCleared = await userDataCascadeWrites.clearFcmTokenForTechnician(userId);
59:    // KYC is nested inside the technician doc â€” hard-deleting the doc removes it too.
60:    technicianHardDeleted = await userDataCascadeWrites.hardDeleteTechnician(userId);
61:    kycHardDeleted = technicianHardDeleted;
62:  } else {
63:    // Customer FCM is topic-based (`customer_<uid>`); no per-doc cleanup needed.
64:    fcmTokensCleared = true;
65:  }
66:
67:  return {
68:    bookings,
69:    ratings,
70:    complaints,
71:    walletLedgerAnonymized,
72:    bookingEventsAnonymized,

211:   * Only the resourceId field is anonymized so the entries remain queryable
212:   * by the operator while no longer linking back to the natural-person uid.
213:   */
214:  async anonymizeAuditLogResourceId(uid: string, anonymizedHash: string): Promise<number> {
215:    const container = getCosmosClient().database(DB_NAME).container(AUDIT_LOG_CONTAINER);
216:    const { resources } = await container
217:      .items.query<Record<string, unknown>>({
218:        query: 'SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.resourceId = @uid',
219:        parameters: [{ name: '@uid', value: uid }],
220:      })
221:      .fetchAll();
222:    let n = 0;
223:    const anonId = `deleted-${anonymizedHash.slice(0, 16)}`;
224:    for (const r of resources) {
225:      const updated: Record<string, unknown> = { ...r, resourceId: anonId };
226:      const id = r['id'] as string;
227:      const pk = (r['partitionKey'] as string) ?? '';
228:      await container.item(id, pk).replace(updated);
229:      n += 1;
230:    }
231:    return n;
232:  },
233:
234:  /**
235:   * Clear FCM token from technician doc (best-effort; customer FCM is topic-based,
236:   * so nothing per-document to clear â€” we return a flag for the inventory check).
237:   */
238:  async clearFcmTokenForTechnician(uid: string): Promise<boolean> {
239:    const container = getCosmosClient().database(DB_NAME).container(TECHNICIANS_CONTAINER);
240:    try {
241:      const { resource } = await container.item(uid, uid).read<Record<string, unknown>>();
242:      if (!resource) return false;
243:      const updated: Record<string, unknown> = { ...resource };
244:      delete updated['fcmToken'];
245:      await container.item(uid, uid).replace(updated);
246:      return true;
247:    } catch (err) {
248:      if (isCosmos404(err)) return false;
249:      throw err;
250:    }
251:  },
252:};

22:/**

24: *
25: * These tests exercise the local-state-first sign-out sequence with MockK mocks for
26: * FirebaseAuth, FirebaseMessaging, IdTokenCache, and DeviceTokenRegistrar.
27: * The existing [SessionManagerTest] covers the prefs + AuthState round-trips via Robolectric.
28: *
29: * Sign-out contract (local-state-first ordering):
30: * 1. prefs are cleared FIRST (survives process kill; prevents stale-uid auth on cold start)
31: * 2. authState transitions to Unauthenticated BEFORE remote cleanup
32: * 3. idTokenCache.signalSignOut() clears cached token and pauses refresh loop (no scope cancel)
33: * 4. firebaseAuth.signOut() is called (best-effort)
34: * 5. firebaseMessaging.deleteToken() is called (best-effort) â€” Step 6b
35: * 6. deviceTokenRegistrar.unregister() is called (best-effort) â€” Step 6c
36: * 7. The sequence completes even if individual steps throw (runCatching resilience)
37: * 8. FCM / device-token cleanup is skipped if generation changes mid-flight (concurrent sign-in guard)
38: *
39: * Note: FCM topic unsubscription (previously Step 6a) was removed in E19-S02. The API
40: * now tracks device tokens directly; [DeviceTokenRegistrar.unregister] replaces topic cleanup.
41: */

64:        every { editor.apply() } just runs

275:export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
276:  const pathname = request.nextUrl.pathname;
277:
278:  // 1. Auth API bypass â€” no locale routing, no JWT check
279:  if (
280:    pathname.startsWith('/admin-api/v1/admin/auth/refresh') ||
281:    pathname.startsWith('/admin-api/v1/admin/auth/login') ||
282:    pathname.startsWith('/admin-api/v1/admin/auth/setup')
283:  ) {
284:    return NextResponse.next();
285:  }
286:
287:  // 2. Strip locale prefix to get the underlying path for capability checks
288:  const rawPath = stripLocalePrefix(pathname, routing.locales);
289:  const hasLocalePrefix = routing.locales.some(
290:    (locale) => pathname === `/${locale}` || pathname.startsWith(`/${locale}/`),
291:  );
292:
293:  if (rawPath === '/') {
294:    const locale = getLocaleFromRequest(request, routing.defaultLocale, routing.locales);
295:    return NextResponse.redirect(externalUrl(request, `/${locale}/login`));
296:  }
297:
298:  if (
299:    !hasLocalePrefix &&
300:    (rawPath === '/login' ||
301:      rawPath.startsWith('/login/') ||
302:      rawPath === '/setup' ||
303:      rawPath.startsWith('/setup/'))
304:  ) {
305:    const locale = getLocaleFromRequest(request, routing.defaultLocale, routing.locales);
306:    return NextResponse.redirect(externalUrl(request, `/${locale}${rawPath}`));
307:  }
308:
309:  // 3. Public paths â€” locale routing only, no JWT required
310:  const PUBLIC_PATHS = ['/', '/login', '/setup'];
311:  if (PUBLIC_PATHS.some((p) => rawPath === p || rawPath.startsWith(p + '/'))) {

5:
6:---
7:
8:## Problem statement
9:
10:Three FCM payloads currently leak PII over public topics:
11:
12:1. **`sendOwnerSosAlert`** (`api/src/services/fcm.service.ts:84-100`) â€” publishes
13:   `customerId + technicianId + slotAddress` to topic `owner_alerts`. Anyone who
14:   subscribes to `owner_alerts` from any app instance reads SOS events.
15:   *(Partially addressed by E11-S05b-2 which trims to incidentId only.)*
16:2. **`sendBookingStatusUpdatePush`** and **`sendCustomerNotification`**
17:   (`api/src/services/fcm.service.ts:5-29`) â€” publish to `customer_<uid>` topics with
18:   `bookingId` + status. A malicious tech-app could subscribe to a known
19:   `customer_<uid>` topic to harvest booking IDs.
20:3. **`sendTechnicianBookingStatusUpdatePush`** and earnings pushes
21:   (`api/src/services/fcm.service.ts:102-115`) â€” publish to `technician_<uid>` topics
22:   with `bookingId` + amount fields. Symmetric leak risk for technician data.
23:
24:**Status:** `not-yet-mitigated`. **Impact:** PII exposure across the wrong-side app
25:(customer reads technician earnings, technician reads customer addresses).

27:---
28:
29:## Approach (chosen)
30:
31:**Switch from topic-based send to device-token send.** Every authenticated session
32:registers its FCM device token with the API; the API stores token-per-userId; pushes
33:target the device token, not the topic.
34:
35:**Topic-based send is retained only for opt-in broadcast notifications** (e.g., "new
36:service category available in your area") where the payload is non-PII.

69:                                                    { userId, deviceToken, platform,

"C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe" -Command 'Get-Content docs/adr/0026-fcm-device-token-vs-topic.md | Select-Object -First 140 | ForEach-Object -Begin {$i=1} -Process {"$i`:$($_)"; $i++}' in C:\Alok\Business Projects\Urbanclap-dup\.worktrees\E19-S02
 succeeded in 957ms:
1:# ADR-0026 â€” FCM Push: Device-Token Send by Default; Topic Only for Non-PII Broadcasts
2:
3:**Status:** Accepted  
4:**Date:** 2026-05-18  
5:**Deciders:** Alok Tiwari  
6:**Supersedes:** Implicit topic-based send pattern used since E11-S05a
7:
8:---
9:
10:## Context
11:
12:The homeservices platform uses Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to push booking status updates,
13:location updates, earnings notifications, SOS alerts, and DPDP erasure notices to Android apps
14:and admin web.
15:
16:The original implementation used FCM topics (e.g. `customer_<uid>`, `technician_<uid>`,
17:`owner_alerts`) for all sends. This pattern was convenient but creates two threat surfaces:
18:
19:1. **I-A2 (STRIDE I)**: User IDs embedded in topic names are visible in Firebase Console logs,
20:   GCP Cloud Logging, and to any app instance that subscribes to a guessed topic name.
21:2. **Topic payload eavesdrop**: FCM topics are subscription-based. A malicious client that
22:   knows a victim's UID can subscribe to `customer_<uid>` and receive all booking-related
23:   pushes, including bookingId, location coordinates, and technician identity.
24:
25:E11-S05b-2 partially mitigated the SOS path by trimming the payload to `incidentId` only.
26:E19-S02 generalises the mitigation to ALL PII-bearing sends.
27:
28:---
29:
30:## Decision
31:
32:**Default: Device-token-based send.** Every authenticated session registers its FCM
33:registration token with the API (`POST /v1/devices/register`). The API stores the token in
34:the `device_tokens` Cosmos container (partitioned by `/userId`). Push functions look up the
35:registered tokens for the target userId and send to those tokens directly.
36:
37:**Narrow exception: Non-PII opt-in topics.** Topic-based send is retained ONLY for messages
38:whose payload contains no user-identifiable data (e.g. `new_service_in_area`, app update
39:announcements). No user IDs, booking IDs, or financial data may appear in a topic-addressed
40:message.
41:
42:---
43:
44:## Token lifecycle
45:
46:| Event | Action |
47:|---|---|
48:| App start / FCM token refresh | `POST /v1/devices/register` |
49:| User sign-out (customer-app, technician-app) | `DELETE /v1/devices/{token}` |
50:| Admin logout (admin-web) | `deleteToken()` + `DELETE /v1/devices/{token}` |
51:| Daily timer (02:00 UTC) | Prune tokens with `lastSeen` > 60 days |
52:
53:---
54:
55:## Consequences
56:
57:**Positive**
58:- Eliminates I-A2 eavesdrop surface: sends are unicast to enrolled devices only.
59:- Owner SOS/shield alerts reach the owner's enrolled admin browsers, not an open topic.
60:- Compatible with FCM `sendMulticast` (up to 500 tokens per request) for future multi-device support.
61:
62:**Negative / Trade-offs**
63:- Zero-token state: if a user signs in but the device registration call fails (e.g. offline),
64:  they will miss that push. Mitigation: `DeviceTokenRegistrar.register()` is also called on
65:  app resume and FCM token-refresh callback, so stale/missing registrations recover on the
66:  next launch.
67:- Stale-token send failures: FCM returns `messaging/registration-token-not-registered` for
68:  deleted or rotated tokens. The prune timer catches 60-day-old tokens; in-flight failures
69:  are logged to Sentry and skipped (do not retry to the same token).
70:
71:---
72:
73:## Alternatives Rejected
74:
75:| Alternative | Reason rejected |
76:|---|---|
77:| Keep topics for all sends | Leaves I-A2 unmitigated; subscriber eavesdrop attack remains viable |
78:| Payload-only trim (no send-path change) | Reduces data leakage in payload but UID-in-topic-name exposure persists in GCP logs |
79:| Instance-group topics (opaque IDs instead of UIDs) | Adds complexity without eliminating the subscription-eavesdrop surface |
80:
81:---
82:
83:## References
84:
85:- `docs/threat-model.md` â€” threat I-A2 (FCM topic payload PII leak)
86:- `docs/adr/0002-fcm-universal-messaging-spine.md` â€” original FCM ADR
87:- `docs/adr/0024-sos-audio-e2e-encryption.md` â€” partial SOS mitigation (E11-S05b-2)
88:- E19-S02 story â€” full device-token migration implementation

+# ADR-0026 — FCM Push: Device-Token Send by Default; Topic Only for Non-PII Broadcasts
+
+**Status:** Accepted  
+**Date:** 2026-05-18  
+**Deciders:** Alok Tiwari  
+**Supersedes:** Implicit topic-based send pattern used since E11-S05a
+
+---
+
+## Context
+
+The homeservices platform uses Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) to push booking status updates,
+location updates, earnings notifications, SOS alerts, and DPDP erasure notices to Android apps
+and admin web.
+
+The original implementation used FCM topics (e.g. `customer_<uid>`, `technician_<uid>`,
+`owner_alerts`) for all sends. This pattern was convenient but creates two threat surfaces:
+
+1. **I-A2 (STRIDE I)**: User IDs embedded in topic names are visible in Firebase Console logs,
+   GCP Cloud Logging, and to any app instance that subscribes to a guessed topic name.
+2. **Topic payload eavesdrop**: FCM topics are subscription-based. A malicious client that
+   knows a victim's UID can subscribe to `customer_<uid>` and receive all booking-related
+   pushes, including bookingId, location coordinates, and technician identity.
+
+E11-S05b-2 partially mitigated the SOS path by trimming the payload to `incidentId` only.
+E19-S02 generalises the mitigation to ALL PII-bearing sends.
+
+---
+
+## Decision
+
+**Default: Device-token-based send.** Every authenticated session registers its FCM
+registration token with the API (`POST /v1/devices/register`). The API stores the token in
+the `device_tokens` Cosmos container (partitioned by `/userId`). Push functions look up the
+registered tokens for the target userId and send to those tokens directly.
+
+**Narrow exception: Non-PII opt-in topics.** Topic-based send is retained ONLY for messages
+whose payload contains no user-identifiable data (e.g. `new_service_in_area`, app update
+announcements). No user IDs, booking IDs, or financial data may appear in a topic-addressed
+message.
+
+---
+
+## Token lifecycle
+
+| Event | Action |
+|---|---|
+| App start / FCM token refresh | `POST /v1/devices/register` |
+| User sign-out (customer-app, technician-app) | `DELETE /v1/devices/{token}` |
+| Admin logout (admin-web) | `deleteToken()` + `DELETE /v1/devices/{token}` |
+| Daily timer (02:00 UTC) | Prune tokens with `lastSeen` > 60 days |
+
+---
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive**
+- Eliminates I-A2 eavesdrop surface: sends are unicast to enrolled devices only.
+- Owner SOS/shield alerts reach the owner's enrolled admin browsers, not an open topic.
+- Compatible with FCM `sendMulticast` (up to 500 tokens per request) for future multi-device support.
+
+**Negative / Trade-offs**
+- Zero-token state: if a user signs in but the device registration call fails (e.g. offline),
+  they will miss that push. Mitigation: `DeviceTokenRegistrar.register()` is also called on
+  app resume and FCM token-refresh callback, so stale/missing registrations recover on the
+  next launch.
+- Stale-token send failures: FCM returns `messaging/registration-token-not-registered` for
+  deleted or rotated tokens. The prune timer catches 60-day-old tokens; in-flight failures
+  are logged to Sentry and skipped (do not retry to the same token).
+
+---
+
+## Alternatives Rejected
+
+| Alternative | Reason rejected |
+|---|---|
+| Keep topics for all sends | Leaves I-A2 unmitigated; subscriber eavesdrop attack remains viable |
+| Payload-only trim (no send-path change) | Reduces data leakage in payload but UID-in-topic-name exposure persists in GCP logs |
+| Instance-group topics (opaque IDs instead of UIDs) | Adds complexity without eliminating the subscription-eavesdrop surface |
+
+---
+
+## References
+
+- `docs/threat-model.md` — threat I-A2 (FCM topic payload PII leak)
+- `docs/adr/0002-fcm-universal-messaging-spine.md` — original FCM ADR
+- `docs/adr/0024-sos-audio-e2e-encryption.md` — partial SOS mitigation (E11-S05b-2)
+- E19-S02 story — full device-token migration implementation

 ### A.4 Information disclosure

36:async function completeTotpLogin(
37:  req: HttpRequest,
38:  adminUser: LoginAdminUser,
39:  role: AdminRole,
40:  totpCode: string,
41:): Promise<HttpResponseInit> {
42:  if (!adminUser.totpSecret) {
43:    return { status: 409, jsonBody: { code: 'TOTP_NOT_CONFIGURED' } };
44:  }
45:
46:  const secret = decryptSecret(adminUser.totpSecret);
47:  if (!verifyToken(totpCode, secret)) {
48:    const _ts = new Date().toISOString();
49:    void appendAuditEntry({ id: randomUUID(), adminId: adminUser.adminId, role, action: 'ADMIN_LOGIN_FAILED', resourceType: 'admin_session', resourceId: adminUser.adminId, payload: { reason: 'TOTP_INVALID' }, timestamp: _ts, partitionKey: _ts.slice(0, 7) }).catch(Sentry.captureException);
50:    return { status: 422, jsonBody: { code: 'TOTP_INVALID' } };
51:  }
52:
53:  const session = await createAdminSession({ adminId: adminUser.adminId, role });
54:  const accessToken = await signAccessToken({
55:    sub: adminUser.adminId,
56:    role,
57:    sessionId: session.sessionId,
58:  });
59:
60:  const ip = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') ?? req.headers.get('x-real-ip') ?? undefined;
61:  const userAgent = req.headers.get('user-agent') ?? undefined;
62:  void auditLog(
63:    { adminId: adminUser.adminId, role, sessionId: session.sessionId },
64:    'admin.login',
65:    'admin_session',
66:    session.sessionId,
67:    { sessionId: session.sessionId },
68:    {
69:      ...(ip !== undefined && { ip }),
70:      ...(userAgent !== undefined && { userAgent }),
71:    },
72:  );
73:
74:  const cookies: Cookie[] = [
75:    {
76:      name: 'hs_access',
77:      value: accessToken,
78:      httpOnly: true,
79:      secure: true,
80:      sameSite: 'Strict',
81:      path: '/',
82:      maxAge: 900,
83:    },
84:    {

86:      // for O(1) lookup in the refresh handler; rawRefreshToken is the one-time
87:      // credential rotated on each use.
88:      name: 'hs_refresh',
89:      value: `${session.sessionId}:${session.rawRefreshToken}`,
90:      httpOnly: true,
91:      secure: true,
92:      sameSite: 'Strict',
93:      path: '/',
94:      maxAge: 28800,
95:    },
96:  ];

105:async function completeChallengeLogin(
106:  req: HttpRequest,
107:  challengeToken: string,
108:  totpCode: string,
109:): Promise<HttpResponseInit> {
110:  const challenge = await verifyMfaChallengeToken(challengeToken);
111:  if (!challenge) {
112:    return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'MFA_CHALLENGE_INVALID' } };
113:  }
114:
115:  const adminUser = await getAdminUserById(challenge.sub);
116:  if (!adminUser || adminUser.deactivatedAt) {
117:    return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'ADMIN_NOT_FOUND' } };
118:  }
119:  if (adminUser.email.toLowerCase() !== challenge.email.toLowerCase()) {
120:    return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'MFA_CHALLENGE_INVALID' } };
121:  }
122:
123:  const role = normalizeAdminRole(adminUser.role);
124:  if (!role) {
125:    return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'ADMIN_NOT_FOUND' } };
126:  }
127:
128:  if (!adminUser.totpEnrolled) {
129:    return { status: 409, jsonBody: { code: 'TOTP_NOT_ENROLLED' } };
130:  }
131:
132:  return completeTotpLogin(req, adminUser, role, totpCode);
133:}

135:export async function adminLoginHandler(
136:  req: HttpRequest,
137:  _ctx: InvocationContext,
138:): Promise<HttpResponseInit> {
139:  let raw: unknown;
140:  try {
141:    raw = await req.json();
142:  } catch {
143:    return { status: 400, jsonBody: { code: 'INVALID_JSON' } };
144:  }
145:
146:  const parsed = LoginRequestSchema.safeParse(raw);
147:  if (!parsed.success) {
148:    return {
149:      status: 400,
150:      jsonBody: {
151:        code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR',
152:        issues: parsed.error.issues.map((i) => ({
153:          path: i.path,
154:          message: i.message,
155:          code: i.code,
156:        })),
157:      },
158:    };
159:  }
160:
161:  if ('challengeToken' in parsed.data) {
162:    return completeChallengeLogin(req, parsed.data.challengeToken, parsed.data.totpCode);
163:  }
164:
165:  const { idToken, totpCode } = parsed.data;
166:
167:  let uid: string;
168:  let verifiedEmail: string | null = null;
169:  try {
170:    const decoded = await verifyFirebaseIdToken(idToken);
171:    uid = decoded.uid;
172:    if (decoded.email && decoded.email_verified === true) {
173:      verifiedEmail = decoded.email.toLowerCase();
174:    }
175:  } catch {
176:    return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'FIREBASE_TOKEN_INVALID' } };
177:  }
178:
179:  let adminUser = await getAdminUserById(uid);
180:  if (!adminUser && verifiedEmail) {
181:    const invite = await getAdminUserByEmail(verifiedEmail);
182:    if (invite && isAdminInvite(invite) && !invite.deactivatedAt) {
183:      adminUser = await claimAdminInvite(invite, uid, verifiedEmail);
184:    }
185:  }
186:
187:  if (!adminUser || adminUser.deactivatedAt) {
188:    return { status: 401, jsonBody: { code: 'ADMIN_NOT_FOUND' } };
189:  }
190:  const role = normalizeAdminRole(adminUser.role);

The patch switches critical push paths to device-token delivery without registering mobile tokens, leaves owner alerts on topics, and has multiple blockers in the admin web token lifecycle. It also misses cleanup paths needed for logout and erasure.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Register mobile tokens before relying on them — C:/Alok/Business Projects/Urbanclap-dup/.worktrees/E19-S02/api/src/services/fcm.service.ts:17-20
  After this lookup replaced the old `customer_<uid>` / `technician_<uid>` topic sends, fresh mobile sessions need to populate `device_tokens` first. In this patch the new `DeviceTokenRegistrar.register()` methods are only exercised by tests and never called from customer sign-in/app start/onNewToken or technician sign-in/onNewToken, so `tokens.length` is 0 and all migrated customer/technician pushes are skipped.

- [P1] Send owner alerts to enrolled admin tokens — C:/Alok/Business Projects/Urbanclap-dup/.worktrees/E19-S02/api/src/services/fcm.service.ts:47-47
  Admin web now registers Web Push tokens in `device_tokens`, but this helper still sends SOS/shield/complaint owner alerts to the open `owner_alerts` topic; no code subscribes the new web tokens to that topic, and ADR-0026 says owner alerts should reach enrolled admin browsers via device tokens. In admin-web deployments relying on the new registration, these alerts won't reach the service worker and topic subscribers can still receive payloads containing booking/technician identifiers.

- [P2] Point admin web registration at the admin device route — C:/Alok/Business Projects/Urbanclap-dup/.worktrees/E19-S02/admin-web/src/lib/push-registration.ts:15-15
  `/admin-api/v1/devices/register` maps to the customer `v1/devices/register` Function, while the admin handlers added here are registered at `admin/v1/devices/...`. With a Firebase ID token this stores the admin browser as a `customer` token and bypasses `requireAdmin`; the DELETE path below has the same mismatch, so the admin device-token lifecycle never uses the admin endpoints.

- [P2] Retry admin push registration after MFA completes — C:/Alok/Business Projects/Urbanclap-dup/.worktrees/E19-S02/admin-web/app/[locale]/login/page.tsx:204-205
  When `postAdminLogin` returns `mfaRequired` or setup-required, this call runs before any `hs_access` admin session exists and `handleLoginResponse` only shows the MFA/setup step; the final MFA submit path does not call `registerAdminPushToken`. For enrolled admins, push registration therefore runs at the wrong point and is not retried after successful MFA.

- [P2] Unregister the old FCM token before rotating it — C:/Alok/Business Projects/Urbanclap-dup/.worktrees/E19-S02/customer-app/app/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/customer/data/auth/SessionManager.kt:214-214
  For a customer who has a registered device token, deleting/rotating the FCM token here after `signalSignOut()` clears the bearer and `firebaseAuth.signOut()` removes the current user happens before `deviceTokenRegistrar.unregister()` below. That unregister fetches the current token and uses the auth interceptor, so it can delete a new/unauthenticated token instead of the server row for the old registered token, leaving the signed-out device eligible for pushes until stale-token pruning.

- [P2] Delete device-token docs during user erasure — C:/Alok/Business Projects/Urbanclap-dup/.worktrees/E19-S02/api/src/cosmos/device-token-repository.ts:64-64
  Adding userId-keyed `device_tokens` creates a new per-user store, but this `unregisterAllForUser` helper is not called outside tests and the existing DPDP erasure cascade still only clears the legacy technician `fcmToken` / treats customers as topic-based. For an erased customer or technician with registered devices, these token docs remain linked to the UID and can still be returned by `sendToUserTokens`.

- [P2] Initialize the messaging service worker on startup — C:/Alok/Business Projects/Urbanclap-dup/.worktrees/E19-S02/admin-web/public/firebase-messaging-sw.js:10-13
  This initializes Firebase only after a page posts `FIREBASE_CONFIG`, but service workers are routinely terminated and later restarted directly for a background push with no page message first. In that scenario `onBackgroundMessage` is never registered and background admin alerts are dropped; initialize from config available at service-worker startup or persist/read the config before handling pushes.
